Author: Techdamentals
Text: $V Worth separating the rails from the lenders this earnings season. A card network moves the transaction and takes a cut of the volume. It does not lend the money. When a borrower stops paying, that is not the network's loss. The bank that issued the card earns interest on the balance and absorbs the loss if it goes bad. Provisions, the cash set aside against loans expected to sour, rose at three separate institutions this quarter. A network carries none of that line, which is why grouping both under financials hides more than it explains. Full explainer, plain English: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hlan3N9D9mU Educational, not advice.

Text: U.S. officials pressed China to expand market access for Mastercard and Citigroup during bilateral meetings in Bangkok this week, according to a U.S. Treasury official. The discussions, led by Deputy Treasury Secretary Francis Brooke, took place alongside G20 finance meetings and the IMF-World Bank annual gatherings, focusing on implementing commitments reached during Chinese President Xi Jinping’s September visit to Washington with President Donald Trump. The talks follow China’s Oct. 13 approval allowing Visa to begin preparations for a wholly owned domestic card-clearing business, with up to one year to prepare before applying for an operating license. Mastercard currently processes yuan-denominated card payments through a local joint venture established in 2024 and is seeking approval to operate independently. Citigroup is pursuing a wholly owned securities license to offer onshore Chinese A-share brokerage, underwriting, research and principal trading services. $MA $C $V
